name: United States, California Vehicle Code 21800-21802 as written (right-hand traffic)
status: draft: the statute's rules in the statute's order, checked against the text of the Vehicle Code on 2026-10-30, not validated on any data. Use it on maps whose junction control is complete. On WOMD maps, junctions without mapped control are mostly controlled in reality, which is why us-california leaves out first_entered and yield_right there.
notes: 21801(a) and 21800(e)(3): a left or U-turner yields to oncoming vehicles close enough to be a hazard; 21800 does not apply between them.
21800(a): a vehicle that has already entered the intersection from a different highway goes first (first_entered, entries more than 1 s apart).

21800(b)(1), (b)(2): on a simultaneous entry, the driver on a terminating highway (T junction) yields to vehicles on the continuing highway; otherwise the driver on the left yields to the driver on the immediate right. The T-junction rule is therefore applied only after first_entered (t_junction is none and ending_road_yields is in the list).

21800(c): all-way stop, simultaneous entry: the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. 21802(a), (c): at a stop sign the stopped driver yields to cross traffic, unless every approach has a stop sign.

21800(d): an inoperative signal is treated as an all-way stop. The CAT code reports a light whose state is unknown as signal-unknown and gives no holder; it cannot tell an unobserved light from one that is dark.
Signalised pairs are decided by the CAT right-of-way code (21451, 21453, 21801 on green).

21453(a)-(c): on a circular red, stop; then a right turn (or a left turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street, which the map cannot tell) is allowed, yielding. A red arrow forbids its movement.

CVC 21950(a): yield to a pedestrian crossing within a marked crosswalk, or an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection (crosswalk 'on', unmarked_crosswalk_at_intersection). 21950(b): a pedestrian may not suddenly leave the curb into the path of a vehicle too close to stop (the screen's stepped_out_late). 21950(c), (d): due care toward any pedestrian in a crosswalk.
CVC 21954(a), (b): elsewhere on the roadway the pedestrian yields to vehicles close enough to be an immediate hazard, and the driver keeps due care (unsignalised_road 'care').

CVC 21451(a): on a circular green, a driver, including one turning, yields to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk; on a green arrow (21451(b)) crossing pedestrians face a red, so only due care. 21453(b): a turn on red yields to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk.
CVC 21952: before driving over or upon a sidewalk (a driveway), yield to any pedestrian approaching on it (sidewalk_crossing).

Turning across a cyclist going straight (a right hook, or a left turn across an oncoming cyclist): a cyclist has the rights of a driver (CVC 21200), so 21451(a) and 21801(a) give it priority over the turner.

CVC 21760(c) (Three Feet for Safety Act): do not overtake a bicycle closer than 3 ft (0.91 m) between any part of the vehicle and any part of the bicycle or its rider; change lanes first where another lane is available (not checked); 21760(d): where 3 ft is impossible, pass slowly and only when it does not endanger the cyclist. No statutory distance for pedestrians (null: the screen's physical fallback).
